issues.legal_issue: A High Court deciding a statutory reference must give final answers to the referred questions and state its reasons, even if the parties agree that its answers will depend on the outcome of other cases.
material_facts: The Tribunal referred three questions to the High Court under the income-tax statute.
The High Court answered all three questions in the negative, following earlier judgments, but stated that its answers were subject to the result of appeals pending in the Supreme Court.
The High Court did not give final answers independent of those other appeals.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in disposing of the reference conditionally; it had to give final answers and reasons, and its answers could not be modified by a judgment in other cases.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 66(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the High Court must decide the questions referred and record its answers with reasons. The parties’ consent cannot make those answers conditional or allow them to be altered by a decision in another case.

predicates.statutory_tax_reference: A tribunal referred questions of law to a High Court for decision in a statutory reference.
predicates.answers_made_conditional: The High Court made its answers dependent on the outcome of proceedings in other cases.
predicates.reasons_not_recorded: The High Court did not state reasons supporting its answers.

issues.definition: When a statutory tax reference has conditional answers or lacks recorded reasons, the High Court must give final answers supported by reasons.

issues.legal_issue: Whether compensation for compulsory acquisition and statutory interest on that compensation are capital gains must be determined by distinguishing their nature on the facts of each case.
material_facts: The company received compensation for compulsory acquisition of land and distributed amounts attributable to that compensation to its shareholder.
The High Court proceeded on the assumption that the entire compensation was capital gain.
The Court noted that compensation for land forming part of a company’s fixed assets is prima facie capital in nature, while statutory interest payable on compensation is income, not capital gain.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had to determine on the facts whether any part of the compensation was capital gain; it could not assume that the entire amount was capital gain, and statutory interest was income rather than capital gain.
issues.legal_principle: The character of compulsory-acquisition compensation must be assessed on the facts; compensation for land forming part of fixed assets is prima facie capital in nature under Senairam Doongarmall v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Assam. Statutory interest on compensation is income and not capital gain under Dr. Shamlal Narula v. Commissioner of Income-tax, Punjab, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Patiala. The question arose in a reference under section 66(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922.

predicates.statutory_tax_reference: A tribunal referred a tax question to a High Court for decision in a statutory reference.
predicates.compensation_for_compulsory_acquisition_: A company distributed to a shareholder an amount attributable to compensation it received for compulsory acquisition of land.

issues.definition: When a statutory tax reference concerns a distribution attributable to compulsory-acquisition compensation, the compensation and any interest must be classified according to their distinct character.

issues.legal_issue: Whether salami received for granting long-term leases is capital gain must be determined on the facts of each case.
material_facts: The company received salami for granting long-term leases and distributed amounts attributable to those receipts to its shareholder.
The Tribunal referred to the High Court whether the shareholder’s receipt was taxable as income from other sources and whether it was dividend.
The High Court answered the questions by following earlier judgments without deciding on the facts whether any salami was capital gain.
issues.conclusion: The High Court had to decide on the facts of this case whether any amount of salami was capital gain.
issues.legal_principle: In a reference under section 66(1) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, the High Court must determine the character of salami on the facts of the particular case; the Court cited no earlier authority for this point.

predicates.statutory_tax_reference: A tribunal referred a tax question to a High Court for decision in a statutory reference.
predicates.salami_received_for_long_term_lease_dist: A company distributed to a shareholder an amount attributable to salami it received for granting a long-term lease.

issues.definition: When a statutory tax reference concerns a distribution attributable to salami received for a long-term lease, the salami must be classified on the facts of that case.

issues.legal_issue: A prior appeal concerning whether a dividend distribution out of capital gains is taxable does not decide whether the underlying capital-gains receipt is taxable as income from other sources when that question was not referred in that appeal.
material_facts: In earlier appeals, the question of law was whether distribution of dividend out of capital gains was taxable.
Whether the capital-gains receipt was independently taxable as income from other sources, not being dividend, was not referred in those appeals.
That income-from-other-sources question was expressly referred in the present case.
issues.conclusion: The Court had not decided in the earlier appeals whether the receipt from capital gains was taxable as income from other sources; that question remained for consideration in this case.
issues.legal_principle: The scope of an appeal is confined to the questions of law raised or referred in it. The earlier appeals addressed the effect of the Explanation to section 2(6A) and taxability under section 12 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, only insofar as dividend distributions out of capital gains were concerned; they did not decide the separate question of taxability as income from other sources under section 12.

predicates.prior_tax_appeal: An earlier appeal concerned the tax treatment of a distribution of dividend out of capital gains.
predicates.other_sources_question_not_referred: The question whether the underlying receipt was taxable as income from other sources was not referred or raised in that earlier appeal.

issues.definition: If an earlier tax appeal concerned dividend distributions but did not include the separate income-from-other-sources question, that question was not decided in the earlier appeal.
